description: Reference dimensions for common LEGO pieces, compiled from public sources. Facts only (names, sizes, dimensions, weights).

conventions.size: BrickLink order: width x length (x height in bricks), in studs. Slopes give the slope direction first. Wheels and tires: diameter x width in mm. Axles, liftarms: length in studs (L). Gears: teeth (T).
conventions.length_mm/width_mm/height_mm: dims_basis says where the numbers come from (see dims_basis_values).
conventions.height_mm: Body height without the stud, for on-grid parts. bbox_mm includes studs.
conventions.bbox_mm: BrickLink 'package dimensions' converted from cm: the part's bounding box, studs included. Published to 0.1 mm.
conventions.weight_g: BrickLink catalogue weight. LEGO does not publish part weights.
conventions.family: Matches the inventory taxonomy families: brick, plate, tile, slope, wheel, window_door, technic, minifig, other.

dims_basis_values.nominal_grid: studs x 8.0 mm across, height in plates x 3.2 mm. Moulded parts are 0.2 mm smaller across (0.1 mm clearance per side).
dims_basis_values.nominal_grid_length: length = L x 8.0 mm; liftarm cross-section 8.0 mm wide, 8.0 mm (thick) or 4.0 mm (thin) tall; axle cross-section from BrickLink's bounding box.
dims_basis_values.name_mm: diameter and width in mm, as BrickLink's part name states them.
dims_basis_values.name_nominative: the numbers in BrickLink's name; BrickLink says numbers without units on wheels and tires are nominal labels, not necessarily measurements. Check bbox_mm.
dims_basis_values.bricklink_bbox: no grid size applies; the numbers are BrickLink's bounding box (studs included).

stud_grid.meaning: Studs on top on the 8 mm grid and stud receptacles underneath; stacks with bricks and plates in whole plate steps.

half_stud_offset.meaning: Sits on the grid underneath, but its top stud(s) are offset by half a stud (4 mm).

grid_bottom_only.meaning: Attaches to studs underneath; smooth top, so nothing clutches on top of it.

sloped_top.meaning: Grid underneath; the sloped face has no studs, so only a flat top row (if any) accepts pieces.

sloped_bottom.meaning: Studs on top on the grid; the underside slopes, so only its flat part attaches below.

partial_grid.meaning: Footprint is on the grid, but only some faces connect (open span, hinge, single stud or leaf).

rotated_grid.meaning: Studs on two faces at 90 degrees; the second face is on a grid turned 90 degrees (stud-on-side).

grid_top_only.meaning: Studs on top; thin, with no stud receptacles underneath.

technic_holes.meaning: No studs: connects through Technic holes with pins and axles. Hole pitch is 8 mm (1 stud), but its thickness is not a brick or plate height.

minifig.meaning: Figure parts: join each other and attach to studs at set points (leg holes, head stud, hands).

off_grid.meaning: Not on the stud grid: mounts on an axle, pin, clip, stem or frame, and its size is not a whole number of studs.

plate_height_mm.note: 1/3 of a brick; without the stud

tile_height_mm.note: same as a plate; no stud, so 3.2 mm is also its overall height

stud_height_mm.note: sources give 1.6-1.8 mm; LDraw uses 4 LDU = 1.6 mm; BrickLink bounding boxes imply about 1.9 mm

clearance_per_side_mm.note: moulded parts are 0.2 mm smaller than the grid in each horizontal direction (a 2x4 is 15.8 x 31.8 mm)

compatibility_tolerance.note: LEGO: dimensions may vary at most 1% for elements to stay connectable

ldu_mm.note: LDraw unit; stud pitch 20 LDU, brick 24 LDU, plate 8 LDU, stud 12 LDU wide and 4 LDU tall
